bc9e958b100312a2e8ce9e1d.reason: The CMS page title and URL are inserted into an HTML label with str.format and then wrapped in mark_safe without escaping, so a stored page title containing markup is rendered as raw HTML on customer-facing forms.
bc9e958b100312a2e8ce9e1d.attacker_input: CMS Page.title / Page.url stored in the database (editable by shop staff) for GDPR consent pages

be5b6a6bdd72202ab71ac90f.reason: For Manager values, the string forms of related objects (e.g. names supplied by users or vendors) are joined and returned without HTML escaping, unlike the Money branch, so the admin picotable renders them as raw HTML and stored XSS is possible.
be5b6a6bdd72202ab71ac90f.attacker_input: User-controlled names or __str__ values of related model objects shown in admin list columns

f595529c9218c94d63abc50e.reason: The failure traceback, which can carry exception messages built from untrusted recipe or data content, is put into the card HTML without escaping, so the rendered step card can run injected script.
f595529c9218c94d63abc50e.attacker_input: failure_traceback (exception text from running an untrusted recipe/data)

f595529c9218c94d63abc50e.reason: The contents of warning_logs.txt are placed inside <pre> in the card HTML without escaping, so attacker-influenced warning text can inject markup or script.
f595529c9218c94d63abc50e.attacker_input: warning_logs.txt contents produced by step execution

d5de10ccb6609cda734b0500.reason: A model artifact loaded via mlflow.pytorch.load_model or a pyfunc model is deserialized with torch.load, which uses pickle, so a malicious model.pth runs arbitrary code when loaded.
d5de10ccb6609cda734b0500.attacker_input: Contents of the model artifact directory (model.pth) loaded via load_model/model URI

d5de10ccb6609cda734b0500.reason: The pickle module name is read from a file inside the model artifact and passed unvalidated to importlib.import_module, so the attacker can choose which module is imported and then used as the unpickler.
d5de10ccb6609cda734b0500.attacker_input: pickle_module_info.txt file contents inside the model artifact

d99e22a75e5f93dde732b508.reason: BaseCard.load runs pickle.load on whatever file sits at the given path (or the card pickle inside a directory), so a crafted card file executes arbitrary code when it is loaded or inspected.
d99e22a75e5f93dde732b508.attacker_input: contents of the card pickle file at the path passed to BaseCard.load (e.g., a recipe step output directory used by BaseStep.inspect)

ff96025ff0b9269363e73380.reason: param_path is built from the attacker-controlled param key; if the key's name validation allows traversal sequences (e.g. '../'), this opens an arbitrary file and leaks its contents through the MlflowException message when the values differ.
ff96025ff0b9269363e73380.attacker_input: param key passed to log_param / log_batch (REST tracking API) reaching FileStore._log_run_param

836e51cd09763fb2f7e40aeb.reason: Contents of warning_logs.txt are inserted unescaped into the card's HTML through the `{{ STEP_WARNINGS }}` template slot, which lacks the `|e` filter applied to the stacktrace, so warning text derived from processed data could inject script into the rendered card.
836e51cd09763fb2f7e40aeb.attacker_input: warning_logs.txt content produced during recipe step execution (e.g., warnings echoing dataset values)

9535832a9aff36b251e60676.reason: The traversal check only rejects filenames beginning with '../', so archive entries such as 'a/../../x', absolute paths like '/etc/x', or Windows '..\' paths are passed to path.joinpath and written outside the extraction directory.
9535832a9aff36b251e60676.attacker_input: Archive entry filenames inside the 7z file being extracted.

9535832a9aff36b251e60676.reason: Symlink targets read from archive contents are created without validation, so a symlink entry can point anywhere and later entries or consumers can then read or write through it.
9535832a9aff36b251e60676.attacker_input: Symlink entry data inside the 7z archive.

2ebba0838cccbd6983e9d1bf.reason: Output paths in target_filepath come from archive member names, and this older vendored py7zr only strips relative-path markers rather than checking that the resolved path stays inside the destination, so a crafted 7z archive (e.g. with '../' segments, CVE-2022-44900) can write files outside the extraction directory.
2ebba0838cccbd6983e9d1bf.attacker_input: filenames stored in the 7z archive being extracted
